title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on the Issue of How an Accounting Firm Shall Bear Liability for Issuing False Capital Verification Certificates for Enterprises

articles.content_en: 1. An accounting firm is a public institution approved by the state to independently undertake certified public accountant business in accordance with law. Issuing capital verification certificates for enterprises by an accounting firm constitutes a civil act implemented pursuant to a commission contract. Pursuant to the provisions of Article 106, Paragraph 2 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, if an accounting firm issues a false capital verification certificate for an enterprise before January 1, 1994, causing losses to the client or other interested parties, it shall bear corresponding civil compensation liability.

2. Although an accounting firm has no direct legal relationship with the contractual parties to the case, in view of the fact that its act of issuing a false capital verification certificate has damaged the lawful rights and interests of the parties, therefore, in the assumption of civil liability, the debtor shall first be responsible for repayment, and for the insufficient part, the accounting firm shall bear compensation liability within the scope of the amount certified by it.
Hereby reply.
